_comment: The one identity lock for the Blunix cat. Every scene prompt = scene text + identity + style_lock. Edit here, bump version, delete raw files to re-roll. Dated notes record drift.
identity: The cat is a slender adult Russian Blue, a real cat on four legs, never posed like a person. Soft, short, plush fur in one solid, even silver-blue-grey: no white patches, no stripes, not a tabby, not black, not a hairless Sphynx. Almond eyes filled with vivid lime-green irises and thin dark pupils, never white or grey eyes. Large, wide-set pointed ears, dark slate-grey nose. Calm, faintly amused, elegant, not cartoon-cute. No collar, no clothing.
style_lock: Flat editorial geometric vector illustration: flat colour shapes, fine minimal linework, slate blue-greys on deep charcoal, lime green only for the eyes and tiny indicator lights, generous negative space, calm and quiet. Plain dark charcoal background. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing anywhere.

hero.prompt: A single cat sitting upright and calm on top of a small stack of three server rack units with tiny status lights, watching over them. Wide composition with the cat and servers to one side and open space.

_log: 2026-09-30 v1 probes: base style drew black outlines and a beige coat (muted cream in colors pulled the coat warm); editorial substyle put a yellow backdrop in; roundish_flat gave a striped tabby with a white bib and a white background. Dropped cream from colors, banned outlines, pushed the flat charcoal ground.

2026-09-30 v2 probes: cutout and segmented_colors held the cat best (slender, solid slate coat, lime eyes, no tabby). Backgrounds are ignored by every substyle (red, blue, purple, pale green), so finish.py drops the full-canvas background path and snaps all colours to the Blunix ramp. Locked vector_illustration/segmented_colors. v1/v2 prompts were silently over the 1000-char limit; shortened identity and style_lock, and generate.py now refuses long prompts.

2026-09-30 v3 review (56 candidates): about half drew white or grey eyes (reject), several drifted toward a hairless Sphynx with bat ears and skin creases, two dressed the cat as a person (proxy-1 standing figures, 404-2 in a suit, at-computer-1 in a shirt), and some added a collar (log-1, held-still-1) or white patches (hero-3 bib, packing-1 blaze, sticker-paw-1 tail). Empty-basket put the cat inside the basket both times. v4 identity: eye colour stated as irises + 'never white or grey', plush fur + 'not a hairless Sphynx', 'real cat on four legs, never posed like a person'. finish.py now also removes large backdrop panels touching three canvas edges, and caps Ink to glints.

2026-09-30 v4 review (27 rerolls): eyes held green on most full-body poses; close front-facing faces (reading-docs, braille, coffee-no, sticker-peek) still drew white or grey eyes, braille-4 added a collar, empty-basket-3 added colour swatches. sticker-loaf never produced a loaf (tunnels, frames) and is dropped from the set. Final round: those four scenes repeat the eye colour inside the scene text.

2026-09-30 v5 review: coffee-no-5 passed. braille-5 dressed the cat in a suit with human hands; braille-6, reading-docs-5 and both sticker-peek rolls still drew grey eyes on a front-facing close face; reading-docs-6 gave the cat human hands. sticker-peek dropped (Watchful uses the key scene). Last roll for braille and reading-docs: three-quarter side view, full body, so the face is small and the eyes read as lime.

2026-09-30 finish.py bug found and fixed: once the Ink cap was tightened to 0.2% of the canvas, it overrode the green pool, so any eye larger than that snapped to light grey. Close-up faces looked grey-eyed in review and were rejected for it (braille, reading-docs, sticker-peek, coffee-no and 404 rerolls were partly spent on this). The raw files had lime eyes all along. Green is now gated on shape instead: eye-like bounding boxes (0.9 to 2.0 wide per tall, under 2% of the canvas) or tiny dots keep green; inner ears (about 0.55) and ruled lines go to slate. All 99 candidates were re-reviewed after the fix.
